title: 2019 HMMT February Team Problem 8
statement:
Can the set of lattice points \(\{(x, y) \mid x, y \in \mathbb{Z}, 1 \leq x, y \leq 252, x 
eq y\}\) be colored using 10 distinct colors such that for all \(a 
eq b, b 
eq c\), the colors of \((a, b)\) and \((b, c)\) are distinct?

solutions.text:
Answer: Yes
Associate to each number from 1 to 252 a distinct 5 -element subset of \(S=\{1,2, \ldots, 10\}\). Then assign to \((a, b)\) an element of \(S\) that is in the subset associated to \(a\) but not in that associated to \(b\). It's not difficult to see that this numerical assignment is a valid coloring: the color assigned to \((a, b)\) is not in \(b\), while the color assigned to \((b, c)\) is in \(b\), so they must be distinct.
